hints.title: When does an edge create a cycle?
hints.body: Add edges one at a time. If the endpoints are already connected through earlier edges, the new edge closes a cycle.

hints.title: Track connected components
hints.body: A disjoint-set structure supports the question 'are these two nodes already in the same component?' almost instantly. Start with every node in its own set.

hints.title: The first closure is the answer
hints.body: Because the graph has exactly one cycle, the first edge whose endpoints are already connected is the last cycle edge in the input, which is exactly the required removable edge.

hints.title: Pseudocode
hints.body:
```
parent = [0, 1, 2, ..., n]

find(x):
    while parent[x] != x:
        parent[x] = parent[parent[x]]
        x = parent[x]
    return x

for (u, v) in edges in input order:
    root_u = find(u)
    root_v = find(v)
    if root_u == root_v:
        return [u, v]
    union(root_u, root_v)

return []
```
